Hi class-prep-agent, please turn my syllabus into a calendar.
15.999 Data, Models and Decisions - Fall 2026
Instructor: Prof. R. Okafor. Class meets Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10:00-11:30, Room E62-276.

Course description
This course introduces probabilistic thinking and data-driven decision making for managers. We cover
probability, decision trees, sampling, regression and optimization, with an emphasis on building
models in spreadsheets and Python and on explaining their results to people who have to act on them.
Every session has a reading that should be done before class; plan on about an hour of reading and
another hour of practice problems per session.

Grading
Problem sets 30%, midterm exam 30%, final project 30%, class participation 10%. Problem sets are
submitted on Canvas by 11:59 pm on the due date. Late work loses 10% per day unless you have talked to
the teaching team beforehand. Collaboration on problem sets is encouraged, but every student writes up
and submits their own answers. The midterm is closed book with one double-sided page of notes.

Office hours
Prof. Okafor: Wednesdays 2:00-3:30 pm in E62-410. Teaching assistants: Mondays and Fridays at noon on
Zoom; the link is posted on Canvas. Email is answered within one business day.

Schedule
Tue Sep 8 - Session 1: Introduction and decision analysis (read Chapter 1)
Thu Sep 10 - Session 2: Discrete probability and decision trees (read Chapter 2)
Tue Sep 15 - Session 3: Random variables and distributions (read Chapter 3)
Friday, September 18: Problem Set 1 due
Thu Sep 17 - Session 4: The normal distribution and sampling (read Chapter 4)
Tue Sep 22 - Session 5: Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests (read Chapter 5)
10/2: Problem Set 2 due
Tue Oct 6 - Session 6: Simple linear regression (read Chapter 6)
Thu Oct 8 - Session 7: Multiple regression and model building (read Chapter 7)
Tuesday, October 13: Midterm exam, in class, closed book
Thu Oct 15 - Session 8: Linear optimization (read Chapter 8)
Final project report due December 11, 2026 by 5 pm

Policies
Laptops are welcome for the exercises we do in class; please close everything else. If you need an
accommodation, contact Student Disability Services and let the instructor know in the first two weeks.
Recordings of sessions are available to students who have an approved absence. Questions about grades
go to the teaching assistants first, within a week of the grade being posted.

Participation
Participation is graded on the quality of contributions, not their number. Cold calls are part of
the course; you can pass once per term without penalty. Short in-class polls count toward
participation and cannot be made up, but your two lowest poll scores are dropped automatically.

Readings
All chapters are from the course reader, available as a PDF on Canvas. Supplementary cases are handed
out in class a week ahead. There is no textbook to buy.
